checks: Every feasible nonnegative Lebesgue density is integrable by the unit mass constraint, and K is bounded. An admissible L is bounded above and strictly away from zero, so ∫ρL is finite and is exactly one by the barycenter constraint.

For p=(d+1)/(d+2), the conjugate exponents are 1/p and d+2. The first powered factor is ρL, the second is L^(−p(d+2))=L^(−d−1). Hölder applies even when ρ vanishes on positive-measure sets or is unbounded. Taking the attained minimum yields ∫ρ^p≤E^(1/(d+2)).

The normalized escort is feasible by the same-wave lemma. Since p(d+2)=d+1, its entropy integral is E^(−p)E=E^(1/(d+2)), so the maximum is attained. The equality condition gives ρL=cL^(−d−1) a.e. and the known unit mean of L under ρ gives c=1/E. This establishes uniqueness without requiring pointwise positivity of all feasible densities.

The frozen feasible class is the ordinary uncapped class. For the centered mark of an interval of length 1/2, L=1 and the optimizer is the constant density 2, which verifies the difference from a unit density cap even at a centroid.

Original 5811f0ad1132ce56 §6 (18) gives the same primal and dual formulas and the attaining escort. The frozen proof adds the explicit a.e. uniqueness check from Hölder equality. The archived source digest matches the frozen provenance.

Its ordinary-body barycenter constraints are imposed on densities bounded by 1 before mass normalization, and its conclusion compares the resulting metronoid with depth regions. The reviewed problem has unit-mass ordinary densities with no cap and a power-entropy objective.
Its domination criterion and capacity bound involve capped finite atomic rows. It does not identify the uncapped ordinary-body maximizer.
